newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian PM Gujral wins trust vote, gets warning.
newsitem.headline: Indian PM Gujral wins trust vote, gets warning.

text.p: India's new prime minister, Inder Kumar Gujral, won a vote of confidence in parliament on Tuesday but got a word of warning from the Congress party, the disgruntled ally which brought down his predecessor.

"Do not treat us as your doormat," Congress leader in the lower house Santosh Mohan Deb told Gujral during the debate. "Regard us as your friend. Try to look after our members. They want honour. They want dignity."

Deb's followers felt they were being ignored under India's previous United Front prime minister, H.D. Deve Gowda. They helped to topple him in a vote of confidence on April 11, but pledged to support a centre-left government under a new leader.
Gujral, 77, was chosen by the United Front as its leader on Saturday and sworn in on Monday.
His victory in the confidence vote had been expected. He had the support of both his 15-party United Front coalition, with 178 votes in the 542-member lower house, and the Congress party with 140.
After more than 10 hours of debate broadcast on national television, Speaker P.A. Sangma announced that Gujral, the fourth prime minister in a year, had won the voice vote.
Gujral was opposed by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party, which with its allies controls 193 votes and is the single biggest party in parliament.
The BJP said Gujral's government would be short-lived.

"It is weaker than the previous administration," former BJP prime minister Atal Behari Vajpayee said, referring to the decision by former finance minister P. Chidambaram's Tamil Maanila Congress party to stay out of Gujral's cabinet.

Former finance minister Manmohan Singh, the Congress party's economic policy advisor, told Reuters that Gujral's tenure hinged on the success of a co-ordination committee set up by the two quarrelling allies to sort out policy differences.
Singh said Congress would not seek any changes in the 1997-98 budget presented by former United Front finance minister P. Chidambaram.
"Reports that we are seeking to change the budget are wrong and baseless," Singh said. "I see no problem in the passage of the budget."
But he said economic policy was one of the key issues to be discussed by the Congress-United Front co-ordination committee, headed by Gujral and Congress president Sitaram Kesri.
"I think the government will last as long as the co-ordination mechanism works, and I hope it works for four years," Singh said moments before Gujral moved the confidence motion in parliament.
